notes: The opening continuation says the proof of equivalence of homotopy categories is not in the literature and qualifies the available full details as just this M.Phil. thesis of F. Hintze at Warwick; part is also said to be in Federer notes on algebraic topology from Brown University, 1962.

The upper block contrasts the cartesian and tensor products of cubical sets, calls the two-product situation a complication, and names Brown-Higgins connections as extra structure for a Dold-Kan theorem. It says realisations with that structure have not yet been worked out, and likewise says the more general cubical-group constructions have not yet been worked out for cubical groups.

At p4 ell8 the writer prefers Dold-Kan to an attribution involving Puppe, gives Kan the Hom formula after describing Dold's version as computational, and attributes a general-additive-category description to Epstein. The article in in a dimension n is actually typed.

The Loday paragraph explicitly qualifies modelling all homotopy types as as yet incomplete. Its proposed role for unit intervals and stack structures is framed by I wonder whether and it may be necessary.

The short entries give and a corresponding. (a underlined), Replace eluding by evading., developed, a p5 ell8,9 suggestion introduced by Maybe it would be better as, and manifold. The suggested quotation has paired opening and closing quote marks and a final full stop outside the closing pair.

The p7 comment names Fritsch and Latch for detailed study of the nerve construction and its relation to homotopy types. The p8 comment calls the middle paragraph interesting and continues with modelling geometric situations and taking the nerve, ending on this page at topological.

math_checks.outcome: Checked the variance and the first two degrees of the printed Hom formula under the usual interpretation of C_N Delta^n as normalized chains and Hom as chain maps, for a nonnegative chain complex C. An order map [m] to [n] induces chains Delta^m to Delta^n, so precomposition gives the required map from degree n to degree m. In degree 0, a map is specified by an element of C_0. In degree 1, with boundary d[e]=v_1-v_0, a chain map is specified by a in C_0 and b in C_1, setting v_0 to a, e to b and v_1 to a+d b. Thus these degrees give C_0 and C_0 direct-sum C_1. This is a limited consistency check, not a proof of Dold-Kan or of the statement for a general additive category; it did not supply or change any printed sign.
